notes: Account summary: Emberfield runs a personalization engine for a portfolio of mid-size ecommerce brands. Looking to move high-volume ranking and conversational personalization to a dedicated inference tier to reduce tail latency and control costs.
Primary ask: committed GPU pool (reserved) that can meet 95th pct latency SLOs at peak traffic and predictable throughput (tokens/sec per tenant) during seasonal spikes.

Workloads: mix of low-latency chat for customer-facing assistants (~50 RPS, target 200-400ms 95th), high-throughput reranking for candidate lists (batch rerank jobs up to 10k qps peak internally), and embeddings for recall/indexing (async).

Model preferences: experimenting with Llama 3 13B and mix of trimmed Llama 2-70B for higher-quality reranks. Interested in quantized variants to reduce footprint but concerned about quality regressions on rerank tasks.

Cost sensitivity: high. Wants to limit monthly spend growth to <30% YoY while improving P95 latency by ~30% vs current multi-tenant setup. Prefers guidance on GPU type (A10/A100/H100), reserved counts, and expected utilization targets.

Security: must be deployed in customer VPC with SAML SSO, full audit logs sent to SIEM, KMS integration for model keys, and contract clause for data residency in us-east-1. Legal started a data residency addendum review (blocker).
Routing/fallback: needs automatic fallback to smaller quantized model when dedicated pool saturated; also wants regional failover between us-east and us-west with <500ms added latency budget.

Notes from 2026-02-23 call (Fireflies ff_2026-02-23_ember-poc-demo): AE Jordan + SE Maya demoed baseline hosted API performance. Customer: 'we see P95 tail spikes during flash sales — need deterministic capacity.' Asked for reserved GPU sizing and expected latency curves for 8k/16k context windows.

Security review 2026-03-03 (ff_2026-03-03_arch-review): CIS baseline ok; legal requested sample SOC2 report and KMS architecture diagram. SE action: upload security deck and KMS integration pattern to Drive (done).
Procurement: procurement loop open. Finance expects final commitment by 2026-06. Procurement asked for SLA language around throughput guarantees and credits for missed SLOs.

Technical constraints: large context lengths matter for long-session personalization (8k and 16k). KV-cache warmup times for repeated sessions are critical to maintain <200ms incremental token latency after warmup.

Quantization concerns: engineering asks for comparison matrix: int8 vs q4_0 vs q4_k_mixed on vendor models; accuracy delta tolerance defined as <0.5% nDCG drop for reranking tasks. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommended profiles and earlier quantization validation harness.

Batching/KV cache policy: wants per-tenant batching window <10ms for chat but more aggressive batching for rerank jobs. Also wants sticky KV cache per user-session pinned to GPU to avoid repeated warmups for frequent shoppers.

SLA negotiation points raised by customer: 1) Define throughput unit (tokens/sec or effective requests/sec). 2) Clarify measurement windows for P95/P99. 3) Define credit formula for missed SLO during seasonal spikes (force majeure carveouts).

POC plan: 2-week dedicated POC. Phase 1 (3 days): baseline throughput and latency profiling on 1 A100 equivalent per shard with smallest quant profile. Phase 2 (7 days): run synthetic ramp (traffic replay of last year's flash sale) to identify contention points, KV cache hit rates, prefix caching effectiveness. Phase 3 (4 days): tune batching windows, quant profiles, and produce cost/latency curves and recommended reserved GPU plan.

Proposed GPU sizing: initial proposal to reserve 6 x A100 for production (estimated sustained throughput for mixed workloads). SE to provide detailed capacity model mapping tokens/sec to GPU counts and expected headroom for 2x burst capacity.

Open engineering questions: how Redwood measures 'reserved capacity saturation' and whether automatic fallback to hosted compatible model is supported without per-request config change. Customer asks for example config snippet and routing policy template.
Decision makers: CTO (A. Chen), Head of ML (Priya Rao), Procurement (S. Martinez). CSM Diego introduced for onboarding and success planning once contract signed.
